content.title: Have You Ever Wondered Why No Crops Grow Without Fertilizers and Pesticides Anymore?
content.subtitle: The alarming truth behind farmers’ lost independence.
content.body:
Have we ever wondered why, just a century ago, people could harvest millions of tons of crops without spraying toxic chemicals on their fields, yet today, many farmers struggle to grow crops without chemical fertilizers and pesticides? Is this simply scientific progress, or is there a hidden global agenda to take control of humanity’s food supply?

From the Father of Chemical Warfare to the Inventor of Synthetic Fertilizers

At the beginning of the twentieth century, German chemist Fritz Haber developed a revolutionary method of extracting nitrogen from the air to produce synthetic ammonia, known as the Haber-Bosch process. His discovery transformed agriculture, earned him the Nobel Prize, and earned him the title “the magician who made bread from air.”

Yet this same man developed chlorine gas for use in World War I, burning the lungs of soldiers in the trenches. Later, Zyklon B, a toxic gas produced by a company associated with his research, was used by the Nazis during the Holocaust to murder millions.

Fritz Haber remains one of history’s most tragic paradoxes: a man who helped feed millions (!) while also contributing to the development of devastating chemical weapons.

The Green Revolution and the Destruction of Soil Fertility

Building on Haber’s discovery, the Green Revolution transformed global agriculture in the 1960s. Chemical companies promoted synthetic fertilizers as alternatives to traditional methods involving manure, compost, and natural nutrient cycles.

Although these fertilizers increased crop yields, intensive chemical farming also contributed to soil degradation. Excessive use can disrupt beneficial microorganisms and damage soil health.

Over time, some farming systems have become increasingly dependent on synthetic fertilizers, resembling a patient who cannot survive without regular injections.

The Hybrid Seed Trap and Farmers’ Dependence

Then came powerful corporations such as Monsanto (now owned by Bayer), Syngenta, and Cargill. They became influential players in agricultural markets, supplying seeds and other farming inputs.

Hybrid and genetically modified (GMO) seeds became increasingly widespread. Many hybrid seeds do not reliably produce the same quality of crops in subsequent generations. Consequently, farmers often purchase new seeds every season.

Some patented GMO seeds also come with restrictions on saving and replanting them. This can make farmers dependent on commercial suppliers for essential agricultural inputs, raising serious questions about their independence and control over food production.

Food Contamination and Pharmaceutical Profits

Today, pesticide residues in fruits, vegetables, and grains are a major concern. Excessive or improper pesticide use can expose people to harmful chemicals, some of which are associated with serious health risks, including cancer.

Meanwhile, chemical companies profit from agricultural inputs, while pharmaceutical companies earn revenue from medicines used to treat illnesses. This raises questions about the consequences of industrial agriculture and the commercial interests surrounding it.

The Goal Is Not Just Profit: Discover the Deeper Agenda

We may think their only objective is to make money. But the reality may be far more complex. Those who hold significant influence over global politics and economics may seek more than financial gains. Their ultimate goal, some argue, is to make humanity completely dependent on them. They want to create a world where we are forced to consume whatever they provide and live under whatever systems they impose, with little freedom to choose otherwise.

What Should We Do in This Situation?

Amid all this destruction, Alhamdulillah, some conscious individuals are still striving to revive natural farming methods without toxic chemicals. Their efforts aim to protect the billions of microorganisms and insects living beneath the soil, preserving their natural habitats and sources of sustenance.

Destroying these tiny creatures means putting the entire ecosystem at risk. As Muslims, we have a responsibility to protect the natural balance of Allah’s creation, embrace a healthier, chemical-free lifestyle, and avoid unnecessary dependence on corporate systems.

Above all, we should strive to place our trust in Allah alone (Tawakkul) while making responsible choices to protect our environment and preserve our independence.

References and Further Reading

  • The Alchemy of Air — Thomas Hager

  • Master Mind: The Rise and Fall of Fritz Haber — Daniel Charles

  • Stolen Harvest: The Hijacking of the Global Food Supply — Vandana Shiva

  • Silent Spring — Rachel Carson
